record.paper_title: Computational issues for linear periodic systems: paradigms, algorithms, open problems
record.original_question: For discrete-time linear periodic systems, can one develop exact or approximate model-matching algorithms for synthesis problems such as controller design, observer design, and fault-detection filter design? The open problem is to obtain effective synthesis methods for these periodic systems within exact or approximate model-matching frameworks.

evidence.quote: For discrete-time systems, we mention the lack of algorithms for computing ... or for the solution of controller/observer/fault detection filter synthesis problems using exact or approximate model matching approaches.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a discrete-time linear periodic system of period $K\ge 1$ given by
$$x(k+1)=A(k)x(k)+B(k)u(k),\qquad y(k)=C(k)x(k)+D(k)u(k),$$
where the matrices $A(k),B(k),C(k),D(k)$ are $K$-periodic in $k$ (i.e. $A(k+K)=A(k)$, etc.). Let $T_{yu}$ denote the input–output operator of such a periodic system, and let $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ be a prescribed (possibly periodic) reference input–output operator.

Develop constructive numerical synthesis algorithms — using either an exact model-matching framework $T_{yu}=T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ or an approximate model-matching framework $\inf\|T_{yu}-T_{\mathrm{ref}}\|$ in a suitable norm (e.g. $\mathcal{H}_2$ or $\mathcal{H}_\infty$) — that solve, for the periodic system above, each of the following:
(a) controller design (find a periodic controller making the closed-loop transfer match $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$);
(b) observer design (find a periodic observer producing an estimate that matches a reference response); and
(c) fault-detection filter design (find a periodic residual generator whose response to faults matches a prescribed reference while rejecting disturbances).

The problem is to provide effective, numerically reliable algorithms (exact when feasible, approximate otherwise) carrying out (a)–(c) for general discrete-time periodic systems.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress exists: model matching for discrete-time periodic systems has been studied via lifting/cyclic reformulation and periodic state feedback (Colaneri et al.), optimal fault-detection filters for discrete-time periodic systems can be obtained via periodic Riccati equations, and geometric and LMI-based methods for periodic fault-detection filters have appeared. However, a unified, numerically reliable algorithmic framework covering exact and approximate model matching for controller, observer and fault-detection filter synthesis of general discrete-time periodic systems is not fully established, so the broad open problem remains only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Model matching for discrete-time periodic systems with time-varying relative degree and order
status_evidence.snippet: Model matching for discrete-time periodic systems uses periodic state feedback via a lifting technique (cyclic reformulation) to transform the periodic system into an equivalent LTI system.
status_evidence.claim: Exact model matching for discrete-time periodic systems has been addressed via lifting and periodic state feedback.

status_evidence.title: Fault detection of linear discrete-time periodic systems
status_evidence.snippet: Optimal fault detection systems for linear discrete-time periodic systems are designed via a compromise between robustness and sensitivity, reduced to solving a periodic Riccati system.
status_evidence.claim: Approximate-matching-style fault detection filter synthesis for discrete-time periodic systems exists via periodic Riccati equations.

status_evidence.title: Fault Detection for Linear Periodic Systems Using a Geometric Approach
status_evidence.snippet: A geometric approach to fault detection filter design for linear periodic systems.
status_evidence.claim: Geometric synthesis methods for periodic fault-detection filters have been developed.
